title: Customs and AusCheck Legislation Amendment (Organised Crime and Other Measures) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change cargo security controls, access to secure airport and seaport areas, and eligibility for a parliamentary law enforcement integrity committee.
It would enable suspension of aviation or maritime security cards, or processing of applications, when holders or applicants face prescribed serious security-related charges.
The card changes would apply to the aviation and maritime schemes only, while separate customs amendments would regulate cargo operators, handlers, information use and brokers.
changes: Cargo terminal operators and handlers would face reporting, physical security and management suitability obligations.
Using Integrated Cargo System information to help a criminal organisation would become an offence.
Customs could impose new broker licence conditions and penalise breaches of specified conditions.
The Deputy Speaker and Deputy President would become eligible for the parliamentary committee overseeing the Australian Commission for Law Enforcement Integrity.
summary.affected: Cargo terminal operators, handlers, customs brokers, security-card holders and applicants, Customs, AusCheck and the specified parliamentary office holders are affected.

speeches.speaker: Anne McEwen
speeches.brief: The Selection of Bills Committee report recommended referring the Australian Jobs Bill 2013, Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill 2013, Private Health Insurance Legislation Amendment (Base Premium) Bill 2013, and Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Bill 2013 to specific committees for inquiry by June 2013, and recommended not referring several other bills including the DisabilityCare Australia Fund Bill 2013 and related tax bills; the report was adopted.
